name: Aleph (OCCRP)
tagline: The global archive of research material for investigative reporting. Follow the money through government records and databases.
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 - Peace Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Heavy US government funding concentration (USAID ~50%) creates editorial-independence risk
USAID veto over senior OCCRP appointments per funding agreement
Funding disruption risk if US government priorities shift

news_articles.headline: OCCRP received nearly half its funding from USAID, with veto over senior appointments

academic_citations: Aleph platform referenced in academic research on investigative journalism tools and open-source intelligence (OSINT) methodologies
awards: 2017 Pulitzer Prize in Journalism (Panama Papers, shared with ICIJ and Süddeutsche Zeitung)

policy_outcomes.description: Panama Papers investigation contributed to resignation of Prime Minister of Iceland Sigmundur Davíð Gunnlaugsson and triggered regulatory responses in multiple countries.
Pandora Papers investigation revealed offshore holdings of world leaders and contributed to legislative scrutiny in multiple jurisdictions.

outcome_methodology: Investigative journalism outcomes tracked through published reports, policy responses, and documented resignations/regulatory actions; methodology relies on journalistic verification and public record documentation
published_performance_metrics: Platform usage statistics and investigation impact metrics published in OCCRP annual reports; specific performance benchmarks not formally published
documented_limitations: Access to Aleph restricted to journalists and activists on case-by-case basis; applications reviewed individually with access typically granted within 72 hours
Depends on document quality and completeness of source datasets
Regularly fetches public records from over 200 online sources but coverage depends on availability of public records in each jurisdiction
failure_modes: Data gaps from jurisdictions with opaque company registries
Risk of political suppression (designated undesirable organisation in Russia)
USAID funding dependency creates structural vulnerability to US foreign policy shifts
curation_criteria: Access granted to journalists and activists case-by-case through application process; government records and public databases are primary sources; regularly fetches public records from over 200 online sources
contributor_governance: MIT-licensed open source; community contributions accepted via GitHub; OCCRP controls platform deployment and access policy
disparity_tracking: No formal disparity tracking; platform access restricted to vetted journalists and activists, limiting transparency on equity of access across regions and demographics
community_ownership: Community-contributed code accepted via GitHub; however, platform access and deployment decisions remain centralized under OCCRP control; no formal community governance structure
controversies: USAID funding agreement reportedly gives US government veto over senior OCCRP personnel appointments, raising editorial independence questions (reported 2024)
Designated undesirable organisation in Russia following investigative work on Russian corruption
political_bias_allegations: Allegations that heavy US government funding skews story selection away from US-based subjects; OCCRP states the funding agreement explicitly bars use of funds for US investigations
legal_regulatory_issues: Designated undesirable organisation in Russia; journalists in several covered countries have faced legal harassment
ai_involvement: Uses AI/ML for document processing and entity extraction within the platform
political_relevance_summary: Confronts threats to digital rights and civil liberties by equipping advocates and the public with information and tools.

movement_building_utility.notes: Provides evidence and data that amplifies advocacy and accountability efforts.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase facilitates replication and adaptation. Already deployed across multiple jurisdictions (multiple countries), demonstrating cross-context adaptability.
